findings.evidence: “What = the decision or impact (1-2 sentences), Why = the minimum context needed to act (2-3 sentences)” and “keep paragraphs to 2-3 sentences; a wall of text hides the ask” are predominantly activation of familiar writing practices. Weighted by section length, the Arguments and Example Usage sections also contribute substantial activation rather than expert-only knowledge.
findings.fix: Keep the recovered formatting rules and example, but strengthen the workflow with task-specific judgment that ordinary email advice misses. For replies containing disputed assertions, explicitly attribute the sender's claim instead of adopting it as fact, then distinguish the user's position from the requested resolution. Consolidate repeated formatting instructions into one authoritative location and record any removed duplicate wording in docs/audit/recovery/compose-email/record.md.

findings.evidence: The purpose tie-break says “use Escalation only when impact, uncertainty and a mitigation are all present; otherwise FYI”, but line 24 separately defines “Status: the delta since the last update, then the risk.” Following the ordered classifier for a routine progress report with no ask, prior unanswered request or escalation conditions leads to FYI, leaving the Status strategy unreachable.
findings.fix: Make Status an explicit reachable branch before the final FYI fallback: classify a progress report without a decision request as Status and lead with its delta and risk; reserve FYI for other informational messages. Preserve the existing Request and Follow-up precedence.
